what_its_for: Avacincaptad pegol is an eye medicine used to slow down the growth of geographic atrophy (GA), which is an advanced form of dry age-related macular degeneration (AMD). Dry AMD is a condition that gradually damages the center of your retina (the back of your eye), which can cause vision loss over time. This medicine helps protect more of your retina from being damaged.
how_to_take: This medicine is given as an injection directly into your eye by your eye doctor (ophthalmologist). It is not something you give yourself at home. You will go to your eye doctor's office or clinic once a month to receive each dose. Your doctor will numb your eye before the injection so you feel as little discomfort as possible. After the injection, your doctor will monitor your eye for any problems before you leave.
dosing: The usual dose is one injection (2 mg) into the affected eye or both eyes, given once every month (approximately every 28 days). Your eye doctor will decide how long you need to continue treatment. Do not skip appointments, as regular monthly injections are important for the medicine to work properly.
missed_dose: If you miss or have to reschedule your monthly injection appointment, contact your eye doctor as soon as possible to set up a new appointment. Try not to go too long between injections. Your doctor will advise you on the best time to reschedule. Do not try to make up for a missed dose on your own.
storage: This medicine is stored and handled by your eye doctor's office — you do not need to store it at home. If for any reason you are given information about storage, keep it in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C and 8°C). Do not freeze it. Keep it in the original packaging to protect it from light. Do not use it if the expiration date has passed.
what_to_avoid: After your eye injection, avoid rubbing or touching your eye. Do not swim or use hot tubs for at least 24 hours after the injection. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery right after the procedure if your vision is blurry — wait until your vision returns to normal. Tell your doctor about all other eye drops or medicines you use, including vitamins and supplements, before starting this treatment.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your eye doctor right away or go to an emergency room if you notice: sudden changes in your vision or loss of vision, increased eye pain, redness, or irritation that gets worse, increased sensitivity to light, seeing floaters (spots or dark strings in your vision), or your eye looks infected (discharge, swelling, crusting). These could be signs of a serious eye infection or other complication that needs immediate attention.
when_it_works: This medicine works gradually over time. It does not restore vision that has already been lost, but it is designed to slow down how quickly the damaged area in your retina grows. You may not notice a dramatic change in how well you see, but it is still working to help preserve the vision you have. Your eye doctor will monitor the size of the damaged area in your retina with regular eye exams to check how well the treatment is working.
special_populations: Older adults (65 years and older): This medicine is commonly used in older adults, as age-related macular degeneration mainly affects this age group. No dose adjustment is needed. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: It is not known if this medicine is safe during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Talk to your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. People with eye infections or other serious eye conditions: You should not receive this injection if you have an active infection in or around your eye, or if you have significant eye pain or redness before your appointment. Always tell your doctor about all your eye and health conditions before each injection.
